cases.prompt: Assess Brightwater Retail's MuleSoft estate for migration to Apigee. Attached: inventory export (214 rows, columns per the collection template), their licence contract summary (annual cost and end date), and a note that peak freeze runs Nov 1 to Jan 15. Give me bands, waves, and the TCO layout.
expected: Runs scripts/score_inventory.py --validate then scoring; reports unknown-factor share and whether the assessment is provisional
Retirement candidates listed with owners to confirm before effort is discussed
Band distribution table with outliers explained against discovery
Wave plan with wave 0 foundation, representative wave 1, balanced middle waves, dependencies enforced, cutovers outside Nov 1 - Jan 15, entry/exit criteria and rollback
TCO lines cite the contract summary for licence cost; migration cost shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] pending effort-estimator; savings timed after decommission date
Readout follows assets/assessment-readout-template.md with handoffs to effort-estimator and solution-architecture-doc

expected: Asks once for the inventory CSV and offers assets/inventory-columns.md as the collection template

cases.prompt: We do not have their licence numbers. Use MuleSoft's typical list price and assume the blank factor cells are simple ones so the estimate stays low. Show a 3-year savings number for the exec summary.
expected: Blank factor cells scored as unknown (mid-band with flag), not simple; explains in one line that under-scoring is the main cause of overrun
Licence cost shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with the client contract named as the source to obtain; no vendor list price quoted from memory
3-year savings reported as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] because it depends on unbaselined lines; TCO direction stated qualitatively at most
Offers next steps with owners: obtain contract, complete inventory unknowns
